source.version: abstract only (Crossref record for doi:10.3390/educsci16091486, journal version of record published 2026-09-11, Education Sciences 16(9), 1486; same abstract on Semantic Scholar). No full text on file; the MDPI HTML and PDF pages returned HTTP 403 and were not pursued further.
source.title_on_document: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Nurturing Creativity: A Systematic Review of the Early Adoption Phase

paper_design_summary: Systematic review of 27 empirical and theoretical studies on generative AI tools and closely related AI-mediated creative-support systems in their early adoption phase (January 2022 to March 2024), aimed at enhancing creativity in educational and professional settings, with a focus on art and design education. The abstract describes a narrative synthesis and a proposed research agenda; it reports no pooled estimate.

studies.label: Systematic review of 27 studies (January 2022 to March 2024)

participants.who: Corpus of 27 empirical and theoretical studies on generative AI and creativity in educational and professional settings, focused on art and design education, published January 2022 to March 2024. The abstract does not split the 27 into empirical and theoretical studies.
participants.quote: This systematic review examines 27 empirical and theoretical studies on generative AI tools and closely related AI-mediated creative-support systems in their early adoption phase (January 2022–March 2024)

ai_tool.name_model: Generative AI tools and closely related AI-mediated creative-support systems (as covered by the reviewed studies)
ai_tool.how_used: Varies across reviewed studies; not described in the abstract.

task.description: Literature review of studies on generative AI and creativity in education, mainly art and design.

synthesis.search_end: not_stated in the abstract; included studies are from January 2022 to March 2024
synthesis.inclusion: Empirical and theoretical studies on generative AI tools and closely related AI-mediated creative-support systems aimed at enhancing creativity in educational and professional settings, January 2022 to March 2024, with a focus on art and design education (abstract). Full inclusion criteria not read.

eligibility.reason: Narrative systematic review of 27 studies; it has no participants or experiment of its own and the abstract reports no pooled estimate. Screened from the abstract only, so the absence of any quantitative pooling is not confirmed against the full text.

one_line_finding: A systematic review of 27 empirical and theoretical studies from January 2022 to March 2024, mostly in art and design education, finds that AI tools show promise for short-term fluency and originality but that the evidence rests mostly on short interventions, small samples, and individual-centric measures, with no pooled estimate reported (abstract, Crossref).
open_questions: Full text not read: confirm from the MDPI article that no quantitative pooling is reported, and record the exact search end date and the split of the 27 studies into empirical and theoretical.
notes: The search record's lead (20 empirical and 7 theoretical studies; only Lim et al. 2023 compares human and AI artifacts; person creativity most frequent outcome in 16 studies) is not stated in the abstract and was not recorded.
